input.question: How long can a single thread of spider silk get before it breaks under it's own weight?
input.ground_truth: Wikipedia says the breaking length of spider silk is 109km (_URL_0_). The breaking length is the length of a uniform wire (thread) of a given material which breaks under its own weight. By tapering the thread (thicker higher up and thinner further down) you could of course get a longer thread.

Okay! Imagine a spider making a super thin, super strong string — that’s spider silk. Now, if you keep making that string longer and longer, at some point it might get too heavy for itself and snap, just like if you stack too many books on top of each other, they might fall down.

But here’s the cool part: spider silk is so strong that a single thread can be really, really long before it breaks from its own weight! If you made a silk thread as tall as a big building, it probably wouldn’t break just because of its own weight. It would have to be *much* longer — like as tall as a mountain or even taller — before it got too heavy and broke.

So, the answer is: **A single thread of spider silk can get super long — much longer than anything we see every day — before it breaks just from its own weight!**
